 The Bangladesh Meteorological Department (BMD) today forecast a slight decrease in day and night temperatures across the country over the next 24 hours, while the weather is expected to remain mainly dry with temporarily partly cloudy skies. 
 The forecast, issued at 9am today (19 October), said an extended area of low pressure lies over the northern Bay of Bengal.
 Faridpur recorded the country's highest temperature at 35.2 degrees Celsius on Sunday, while Tetulia recorded the lowest at 19.2 degrees Celsius today.
 Keep updated, follow The Business Standard's Google news channel
 In Dhaka, winds are blowing from the north or northeast at 5 to 10 kilometres per hour. Relative humidity was recorded at 74% at 6am.
 No rainfall was recorded anywhere in the country in the 24 hours until 6am today.
 The sun will set in Dhaka at 5:29pm today and rise at 5:58am tomorrow.
